definition: A language model specifically trained or prompted to perform extended, deliberate reasoning steps before producing a final answer, often using substantial test-time compute.
details: Reasoning models trade off higher inference cost and latency for improved accuracy on complex tasks like mathematics, coding, and multi-step logical problems, compared to models optimized purely for fast, direct responses.
story: Imagine a factory floor where each workstation can glance at every other workstation before doing its part. Think of it this way: A language model specifically trained or prompted to perform extended, deliberate reasoning steps before producing a final answer, often using substantial test-time compute. And here is the clever part: Reasoning models trade off higher inference cost and latency for improved accuracy on complex tasks like mathematics, coding, and multi-step logical problems, compared to models optimized purely for fast, direct responses. Structure decides what the model can even express — the blueprint before the bricks. And that shape of the machine — Reasoning Model — is what makes everything else possible.
